1. بالنظر فى الحادثه الاتى شرحها فيه
  2. الشريف على قاعدة مذهبه الشريف
  3. سيدنا ومولانا قاضى القضاة المنده [باسمه اعلاه]
  4. ادام الله تعالى ايامه الزاهره وجمع له ىىں [دنياه والاخرة]
  5. واحسن اليه وزاد علاه بكشف
  6. ذكرهما ووصفهما وتحديدهما فيه وتوجه
  7. النواب فى الحكم العزيز الحنفى وغيرهم 
  8. كل من المعلم ابراهيم بن محمد بن شرف الدين
  9. الشهير بالسّكرى والمعلم نور الدين على بن المعلم
  10. خليل بن نور الدين على المهندس ايضا المعروف
  11. بابن بيسار وهما من ارباب الخبره والمعرفه بالعقار
  12. والابنية وعيوبها المندوبين لذلك من
  13. الشريف الى حيث الكںيستين الموعود بذكرهما 
  14. بمصر المحروسه بخط قصر الجمع [الاولى المعروفة]
  15. بالعراقيين بجوار المعلقة والثانيه [المعروفة بالـ . .]
  16. بالقرب من الاولى كشفنا كشفا [صحيحا]
  17. فدل الكشف على ان الكنيسه الاولى المعروفه
  18. بكنيسه العراقيين تشتمل على واجهه
  19. بها باب يدخل منه الى سلم يصعد عليه الى [اعلى]
  20. منه الى باب مربع يدخل منه الى ساحه بها تجاه الى
  21. بها فتحه بين كتفين درعها ستة اذرع 
  22. بذراع العمل بها قاعدتين رخاما مزمنة البنا
  23. مهما فى ثلث الفتحه المذكوره عرض كل كتف
  24. من وجهه دراع واحد وثمن دراع بدراع العمل
  25. وارتفاعه من وجه الارض الى معالم يشتمل
  26. الاطرف فيه اربعة اذرع يعلوهما معالم
  27. بملو الفتحه المذكورة كان البستل المذكور
  28. الكتفين المذكورين وعلى عامودين رخاما [كانا]
  29. على القاعدتين الرخام المذكورىں وجد هناك
  30. رخاما مرمىىں ذكر انهما العامودان اللذان كانا
  31. البستل المذكور حرق البستل المذكور [و.....]
  32. علوه وسقط العامودان المذكوران ارتفاع البستل
  33. مع ما تهدم علوه من البنا دراع واحد ونصف ذراع
  34. فى وسع الفتحه المذكورة يعلو ذلك الطرف خشب
  35. محمولة على خشب الشد ويعلو ذلك فى وسط
  36. ارتفاعه ذراعين فيكون الهدم مع ارتفاع الىسىل
  37. ثلاثه ادرع ونصف ذراع وثمن دراع المائل من الحا
  38. الكتفين فى عرض الكتفين كل ذلك بذراع العمل
  39. العامودين المذكورين الى ما كانا عليه ووضع ىساىل
  40. عما حرق واعاده البنا المستهدم لما كان عليه
  41. المذكورة على يسره الداخل ايوان بصدره جنب
  42. هدمت مساحتها ثلاثه ادرع ونصف دراع وسعها
  43. عرضه دراع ورىع دراع وسعها كتف عرضه دراع
  44. ذراع فى دراعين استغماقه ربع ذراع وسمكه
  45. يحتاج الى هدم ذراع زائد على الثلاثه ادرع ونصف
  46. المذكوره وبنا ذلك عرضها من سفلها ثلاىه ادرع وا[لى]
  47. اربعة ادرع ونصف دراع وبجانبها مرمه اخرى 
  48. وارتفاعها ذراعين ونصف ذراع كل ذلك بذراع العمل
  49. الى ىںصىڡ دلك وبنائه واعادته الى ما كان عليه
  50. بالصفه التى هو علىها الان خشى من الضرر وهذه الكنيسه
  51. تعرف بكنيسه الرىاىىن بحدره اليهود ومحيط بها [.....]
  52. ارىعه القبلى ينهى الى الزقاق داخل الكںىسه
  53. الدى هناک وفىه الباب وبعضه الى اوقاف اليهود
  54. وبعضه الى الخراب والحد الىحرى

  56. الزقاق الذى فيه الكنيسه المذكورة بعضه [الى اوقاف]
  57. اليهود والحد الغربى ينتهى الى الخراب بالكنيسه
  58. المذكورة مرمات لم تذكر فى هذالكشف(!) واما الكنيسه

  60. فانها داخل خوخة تعرف بخبيصه تشتمل على واجهه مزمنه البناء
  61. بدخل منه الى الكنيسه المذكوره وبالكنيسه المذكورة على
  62. الصاير بها ايوان بغير سقف به عامودين رخاما احدهما على 
  63. الداخل اليه به ميلة يحتاج الى اقعاده واعادته على ما كان
  64. وبه نفحه قد سقط بعضها وبعضها الى منداع الى السقوط
  65. درعها عرضا ثلاثه ادرع وثلثا دراع وربع دراع وارتفاعها
  66. من جهة الزاوىه دراعىن ونصف ذراع ومن وسط الجنب خمسه ادرع
  67. وىلىا دراع وىها اىصا مٯدار ذراع من سفلها من الوسط
  68. يحتاج الى عمارىه ومرمته وبالايوان المذكور على يسره الصالون
  69. مرمر بالزاويه درعها عرضا دراعين وربع دراع من اعلاها
  70. مں اسفلها وارىڡاع ىلاىه اذرع ونصف دراع ومرمه [يحتاج]

  72. منها على يمنه الصاير بها ىدخل منه الى خربه بها جنب على ىمىں الداحل
  73. الىها به ىاب ومرمه درعها من الباب المذكور دراعىں وثلث
  74. وارىڡاعها دراعىں وىالخزىه المذكوره كتف ٯد هدم
  75. كان حاملا لىسىل هو الان محمول على خشب الشد دراع الكتڡ
  76. المدكور عرصا ىلىا دراع وارىڡاعه خمسه ادرع محاںىه مرمه عرصها
  77. نصف دراع وارىڡاعها دراعىں وںصڡ دراع كل ذلك بدراع العمل
  78. كل دلك الى العماره والترميم ومتى ترك بالصڡه الى هو علها الان حصل
  79. مںه الصرر وىحىط ىهده الكںىسه حدود ارىعه
  80. الحد الٯىلى ىںىهى الزقاق بخوخه خبيصه والحد
  81. الىحرى الى الطرىٯ وڡىه الباب والحد السرٯى
  82. ىںىهى الىىٮ ىعرڡ ىاىن المعرص والعطار وعىرهما والحد العرٮى
  83. ىںىهى الى دار ىعرڡ ٮالٯںدٯ وٯڡ صعالىك الىهود
  84. هذا ما دل علىه الكسڡ والمشاهده والامر ڡى دلك
  85. محمول على ما يقتضيه الشرع وذلك فى اليوم المبارك [التاسع]
  86. والعشرين من سهر رىىع الاول عام ثمانيه وسبعين وثمانمايه
  87. ثم ڡى اول شهر رىىع الاخر من السںه المدكوره فاوص المـ
  88. السرىڡه سرڡها الله ىعالى وعطمها وحلد ملك مالكها

  90. واعلاه وزاد علاه فى امر الكںىسىىن المذكورىن اعلاه ڡىه

  93. شفاها بالںوحه الى حىٮ الكںىسىىن المذكورىں اعلاه
  94. والعمل ڡى دلك بما ىٯىصىه السرع السرىڡ على ٯاعده مذهىه
  95. السرىڡ فتوحه سيدںا ومولانا ٯاصى الٯصاه المںوه
  96. ىاسمه الكريم ىاعالىىه ادام الله ىعالى ايامه واعر احكامه ڡراد معالىه
  97. وصحبته من ىصع اسمه احره مں الساده النواب فى العرىر وعىرهم

  99.  وكشفتا بحصوره كشفا شافىا فوجدتا بالصفر المشروحه
  100. اعلاه ڡعںد دلك استخار الله سىحاںه وىعالى الدى
  101. ما خاب مستحيره واستجار بحرم كرمه الدى مستجيره
  102. لىاںىه ڡى الحكم العزيز هو سيدنا العبد الفقير الى الله تعالى

  107. من جمله من حضر الكسف الاول والثانى المشروحىن اعلاهـ
  108. وثبت لدى سىدںا الىد الفقير الى الله تعالى الشيخ تقى الدين

  122. من التعرض لما اعيد من المرمات بالكنيستين المذكورتين اعلاه

1. ...  order to look into the case which is reported below ...
  2.  the holy law according to the exalted school ...
  3. our master and our leader, the chief Cadi who is mentioned (by name above),
  4. May Allah the most high prolong his illustrious days and make him enjoy (both this world and the next)
  5. and do well by him and increase his dignity. An inquiry should be made (into the two Synagogues which should give)
  6. an account of them and a description of them and their boundaries (or, of that which has been renewed in them). Then went
  7. the delegates of the excellent Hanefite law, and others,
  8. all of them: to wit, the learned Ibrahim ibn Mohammad ibn Sharaf al-Din,
  9. known as al-Sukkarī, the learned Nūr-al-Dīn ʿAlī son of the learned
  10. Khalīl ibn Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī, the architect, known also
  11. as Ibn Baisār, leading men of information and knowledge in regard to real property,
  12. buildings and their defects, who had been delegated for this purpose by
  13. the exalted one, to the place where are the two Synagogues which are known by the description of them
  14. in Fostat—May God protect it!—in the quarter of Ḳaṣr al-Jamʿ, (the first one known)
  15. as that of the Babylonians, near to the Muʿalaḳah and the second one (known as that of the Palestinians)
  16. not far from the first. Now, we have made a thorough investigation,
  17. and the investigation has shown that the first Synagogue known
  18. as the Synagogue of the Babylonians contains a façade,
  19. in which is a gate through which one goes to a ladder, upon which one mounts to (a place higher)
  20. than it, to a square gate through which one comes upon an open space, opposite to which is ...
  21. In this there is an opening between two buttresses, the length of which is six cubits
  22. according to the ordinary cubit. In it are two pedestals of marble erected long ago.
  23. Now, these are at about one-third of the above-mentioned opening. The width of each buttress
  24. on its face is one cubit and one-eighth, according to the ordinary cubit.
  25. Its height, from the surface of the ground up to as far as that part which contains
  26. the laterals, is four cubits. Above this was something still higher...
  27. In the middle of the aforementioned opening is the aforementioned tower ...
  28. the two buttresses aforementioned; and upon the two marble pillars (which were)
  29. upon the two pedestals of marble aforementioned there are found the
  30. two restored pieces of marble. It is said that these are the two pillars which made up
  31. the aforementioned tower. The aforementioned tower had been burned down (and ...)
  32. its upper part, so that the two aforementioned pillars had sagged. The height of the tower
  33. in addition to the top part of the building which had fallen into ruins was a cubit and a half.
  34. Now, throughout the whole length of the opening aforementioned there were laterals of wood
  35. resting upon wooden beams. In the middle
  36. of its elevation it reached two cubits—so that the destruction, taking account of the height of the tower, reached
  37. three cubits and a half and an eighth of a cubit, taking into account the sagging ...
  38. the two buttresses along the width of the buttresses. This computation is on the basis of the ordinary cubit (regarding)
  39. the two aforementioned pillars up to that upon which they rested. And (it is necessary) to replace the towers
  40. to that which they were before they were burned and to rebuild the building which had been destroyed to that which it had been
  41. as aforementioned. To the left, as one enters, is a roofed porch, the front porch of which
  42. has been destroyed up to three and a half cubits in length,
  43. and one and one-quarter cubits in width. Its depth has been uncovered
  44. one cubit by two. Its depth was a quarter of a cubit. The height
  45. needs a tearing down amounting to one extra cubit above the three and a half cubits.
  46. aforementioned. (It will be necessary) to rebuild this whole space from the bottom up three and a half to
  47. four cubits and a half. At the side (of this whole space) is another postern.
  48. Its height is two and a half cubits—all on the basis of the ordinary cubit.
  49. (It is necessary) to clean this up, to rebuild it and to restore it to its original form.
  50. In the condition in which it is now there is danger of injury occurring. Now, this Synagogue
  51. known as the Synagogue of the Rabbanites is in the Quarter of the Jews. (The whole property) can be described according to the four
  52. (cardinal points). The South reaches up to the little street in the Synagogue Enclosure
  53. which is there. In it there is the gate. A part of it belongs to the Waḳf of the Jews
  54. and a part to waste ground. The northern side ...
  55. In this there is a wall about to tumble down. The Eastern Side reaches (unto)
  56. the small street in which is the aforementioned Synagogue, a part of which (belongs to the Waḳf)
  57. of the Jews. The western side reaches the waste ground in the aforementioned Synagogue Enclosure.
  58. Repairs in regard to this are not mentioned in the investigation. Now, as regards the Synagogue 
  59. known as that of the Palestinians—it is also known as the Synagogue of the Rabbanite Jews—
  60. it is inside the passage known as Khabīsah. It contains a façade built long ago.
  61. From it one enters the aforementioned Synagogue. And in the aforementioned Synagogue for one 
  62. who passes through it, there is a porch without a roof. In it are two pillars of marble; one of which to (the right)
  63. of the person as he enters. This is leaning to one side. It must be put in order and placed in the condition in which it was.
  64. In it is a large window, a part of which has already fallen, and a part of which is on the point of falling.
  65. Its size in breadth is three and one-third cubits, plus one quarter cubit; its height
  66. at the corner is two and a half cubits. On the middle of its side it is five cubits
  67. and two-thirds of a cubit. Now, for the space of a cubit from its lowest part up to the middle of it also
  68. needs rebuilding and restoring. In the aforementioned porch to the right of the reception room
  69. is a granite column in the corner; its measurement is in width two and one quarter cubits from its top
  70. to its bottom, in height three and one-half cubits and its restoration (is necessary)
  71. to the same amount in the mortar.  Now, in the aforementioned synagogue the roof is broken in and a door leads
  72. from it lying to the right of one who goes through it. From this door one enters into a place that is in ruins, one wall of which lies to the right as one enters.
  73. In it there is a door. The area needing repairs from the aforementioned door on is two and one third cubits.
  74. In height (this area) is two and one quarter cubits. Now, in the aforementioned chamber, the wall has fallen into ruins.
  75. It used to carry a tower. At the present time it is resting upon connecting beams. The extent of the wall
  76. aforementioned is two-thirds of a cubit in breadth and its height is five cubits. Next to it is a space needing repairs, the breadth of which
  77. is one-half a cubit and its height two and one-half cubits. All these cubits are the current cubits.
  78. All this stands in need of reconstruction and repair. If it is left in the condition in which it is at present, there may happen
  79. through this accidents. The following four boundaries will give the position in which this Synagogue lies.
  80. The south side reaches unto the market-place in the passage Khabīsah; the northern
  81. side reaches unto the street. In it is the gate (to the Synagogue). The eastern side
  82. reaches unto the house known as that of Ibn al-Muʿarrid and of al-ʿAṭṭār and of the others beside them. The western side
  83. reaches unto the dwelling compound known as the Hospice—a Waḳf for the poor of the Jews.
  84. This is what the investigation and the survey have clearly indicated. As for that which should be done in this matter
  85. that is left to that which the Mohammedan law may require. This occurred upon the blessed day (... the nine)
  86. and twentieth of the month Rabīʿa I in the year 878.
  87. Then, on the first day of Rabīʿa II in the aforementioned year, gave over ...
  88. the glorious, may Allah the most High grant them fame and give them strength and prolong the rule of their head-officer
  89. as well as the chief Caḍi ... whose excellent name is mentioned above—May Allah exalt him
  90. and elevate him and increase his grandeur—in the matter of the two Synagogues mentioned above ...
  91. the final decision (?) to our excellent lord and master the chief Caḍi who is named above
  92. by his excellent name—May Allah prolong his flourishing days, do well by him and make his grandeur increase.
  93. He gave orders orally to go where are the two Synagogues mentioned above
  94. and to deal with this matter in harmony with the dictates of the holy law according to his excellent
  95. school (of law). Then went our lord and master, the chief Caḍi, who is mentioned
  96. by his excellent name above—May Allah the Most High lenghthen his days, give strength to his judgments and increase his dignity—
  97. accompanied by those of his colleagues who place their names at the end of this document, those stationed in the honored court of justice and others, 
  98. as well as the architects mentioned above, to where the two above mentioned Synagogues were.
  99. A thorough investigation was made of them in his presence, and the two were found to be in the condition mentioned
  100. above. Thereupon Allah was consulted—praised and exalted be He—who
  101. would not disappoint anyone consulting him; and h was asked of Him, whose kindness is never asked in vain—
  102. for enlightenment in the honoured court of justice (by the chief Cāḍi) our lord, the poor servant of his master Allah the Most High,
  103. the learned Sheikh Taḳī-al-Dīn, the honoured one among the wise and (by) the most respected Mufti
  104. of the Mohammedans Abū-al-Ṭayyib Muḥammad ibn al-Mukri al-Zujjāji al-Ḥanafi, head judge
  105. in the country of Egypt. May Allah the Most High confirm his judgments and give him enlightenment in (the investigation concerning)
  106. the two synagogues aforementioned and their ruins in a legal manner, 
  107. (made) by all those who were present at the first and second investigations, explained above.
  108. Now there was verified before our Master, the poor servant of Allah the Most High, the Sheikh Taḳī-al-Dīn
  109. who is licensed (to deal with legal matters and) to whom reference has been made above—May Allah the Most High confirm his judgments and favour him with the legal proofs—
  110. the contents of the examination that has been noted above according to that which has been put down and explained
  111. above—a veritable legal decision on the fourth day of the month
  112. Rabīʿa II mentioned above in the aforementioned year. Then, after this
  113. there went our Lord, the servant who looks for the aid of Allah the Most High, the Sheikh Taḳī-al-Dīn
  114. the judge who is licensed (to deal with legal matters and) to whom reference has been made above—may Allah the Most High strengthen his judgments—
  115. together with those who are placing their names after his—leaders and authorities in the excellent tribunal and others beside them (to)
  116. the two Synagogues aforementioned. The restorations mentioned above
  117. were found to have been made and (the Synagogues) had been put into the same condition in which they had been (previous to)
  118. the destruction and burning. Nothing whatsoever had been added. It was found also that that which had been restored
  119. was the portion belonging to the Jews. Its restoration and its replacement had been done in a legal manner. This was made clear
  120. efore our master the wise man who has been referred to (above) may Allah the Most High confirm his judge—
  121. ments and favour him with legal proofs, which are acceptable, certain, true, lawful and (impossible)
  122. of contradiction in regard to that which had been restored in the two above mentioned Synagogues
  123. belonging to the Jews—a lawful restoration, as has been explained above,
  124. without any addition to this ... true, lawful, complete,
  125. determined by law, demanded by it and fulfilling the terms of the law
  126. upon the basis of a perfectly legal demand and after the establishing of full proof, and after full legal
  127. consideration had been given with much erudition of the view opposite to this. A proper (document was drawn up)
  128. in regard to this matter on the blessed day, the twenty-ninth of al-
  129. Ḥarām at the end of the year 878. May Allah bless
  130. its end, and may His kindness be for the rest of the prophets and apostles
  131. altogether, and may there be peace! God is sufficient unto us and an excellent guardian!
